findings.defect: Residual DAT-001. The repair says the authoring pass cannot approve itself and that Class O acceptance is Owner or an Owner-designated approver other than the Builder/authoring pass. It then makes the task's recorded acceptance_authority controlling, while AUTO may create and update tasks. Nothing requires that designation to be a verbatim Owner utterance or an already-merged Owner record. Bootstrap allows the same seat to take a later declared non-Builder pass, and the AUTO no-self-certification rule only says a pass is not evidence for itself. On protected main, the only recorded acceptance_authority values are OWNER on Class F tasks; every other task is UNCLASSIFIED_LEGACY and cannot resume until a seat assigns both a class and an acceptance_authority. That assignment is the routine task edit this policy still tells AUTO to perform. 'Acceptance authority is never implied by AUTO' does not stop the seat from writing the field.
findings.consequence: A fresh AUTO seat can record Supervisor, Independent Critic, or another non-Builder role as acceptance_authority, inhabit that pass, and thereby satisfy the 'already accepted' precondition for its own work. Gate 8's Owner-designated approver is then author-recorded rather than Owner-recorded. Invariant 11 is not held in operation.
findings.smallest_repair: State that a non-Owner acceptance_authority is valid only when a verbatim Owner utterance already on protected main names that approver for that task. The authoring seat cannot set, change, or perform it, including through a later pass. Initial assignment of acceptance_authority is outside the delegated lane.

findings.defect: Residual DAT-004. Delegated merge is limited to heads the policy calls Class O, and Class F/S are excluded by name, but class is not bound to Blueprint section 11 substance of the whole diff. An author-written change_class is enough, and label/substance conflict does not fail closed. The content exclusions omit Class S schemas and core interfaces, Class D, and canonical current.yaml keys other than the five listed semantics. law_precedence, current_architecture, role_bootstrap, active_task_id, and active_workstream can change without being a phase, acceptance_authority, exact-next-action, blocker, or Foundation-gate edit. Changing active_task_id switches which Class F/OWNER gate is live without editing those fields. The law-router sentence is narrower still: it excludes only 'Class F/S changes and governed state/task gate changes,' so a cold start can treat next-action, blocker, and pointer edits as non-gate clerical work. 'Reconcile permitted state' and 'create/update bounded tasks' remain affirmative powers beside that list.
findings.consequence: The seat that wants the lighter lane classifies the head Class O and merges Class S/D substance or canonical control-state changes, including a silent switch of the live task, law pointer, or next action, while Foundation tasks on main remain Class F with acceptance_authority OWNER. Invariants 12 and 13 are not held against that head.
findings.smallest_repair: Bind class to Blueprint section 11 substance of every part of the exact-head diff; if the recorded label disagrees, fail closed and do not use the lane. Exclude any head that touches state/current.yaml, state/tasks.yaml, the active handoff NEXT ACTION, law, blueprint, bootstrap/role power, or a canonical pointer. Repeat that boundary in the law-router sentence. Delete 'reconcile permitted state' as a merge power.

findings.defect: Residual DAT-003. Verbatim full SHA, packet blob SHA, prohibition on adding a missing SHA, and expiry when the head changes are confined to 'Owner-reserved gates.' The lane this policy actually auto-merges is non-reserved Class O. For that lane the policy only says a non-Builder authority may use 'the governed exact-head acceptance mechanism defined by the task/law,' and neither the task registry nor the Blueprint defines one. Class O Owner acceptance is not on the reserved list and is not covered by that non-Builder sentence. The ban on post-hoc binding applies only 'where exact-head Owner acceptance is required,' which this policy does not require for Class O. The operating text tells the seat that Owner approvals happen in chat and that Owner need not copy head/blob identifiers. 'When a frozen packet is part of the gate' lets the seat decide the blob SHA is not required. The law-router paragraph does not state the binding rule. Bootstrap still says that if Owner skips a step, state one risk sentence and continue, and this policy does not explicitly supersede that sentence.
findings.consequence: On the delegated lane, a chat approval that names no commit can be recorded by the Total Architect against whatever head is current, and a frozen packet's blob SHA can be omitted. On a reserved Foundation or Master Blueprint gate, a fresh seat can treat a missing SHA as a skipped clerical step under bootstrap and the 'copy identifiers' bullet, then merge. Current state still blocks Foundation final acceptance on OWNER. That is fabricated or post-hoc Owner acceptance, which invariant 13 forbids a delegated policy to weaken.
findings.smallest_repair: Use one binding rule for every acceptance the Total Architect records or merges, including Class O: the acceptor's own utterance must already contain the full head SHA; if any frozen packet was produced for that head, the utterance must contain that packet blob SHA; a missing identifier is a stop, not a clerical copy; bootstrap 'skip a step and continue' does not apply; a new head expires the acceptance. State that rule in the law-router sentence. Rewrite the 'copy CI/head/blob identifiers manually' bullet so it cannot mean inserting identifiers the utterance lacks.

findings.defect: The mandatory stop bullet still forbids 'enabling autonomous merge' with no 'general' qualifier. The new sentence restates that stop as 'enabling general autonomous merge' and says the delegated policy does not supersede it, but it does not explicitly supersede or rewrite the stop bullet. Same-level conflict requires explicit supersession.
findings.consequence: A strict seat can fail-closed the whole Class O lane as itself enabling autonomous merge. A loose seat can treat the added word 'general' as a silent narrowing. This wording drift does not by itself grant Class F/S merge. It is not a material defect if the fail-closed reading is followed.
findings.smallest_repair: Rewrite the stop bullet so the prohibited act is autonomous merge beyond clerical merge of an already-accepted Class O exact head under the delegated policy, and mark that sentence as an explicit supersession of the unqualified stop.
